triplets.head: Pre-myopia (IMI definition)
triplets.tail: SER ≤ +0.75 D and > −0.50 D in children with risk factors

triplets.head: Pathological Myopia (IMI definition)
triplets.tail: Excessive axial elongation causing posterior-segment structural changes

triplets.head: Conventional RGP Lenses
triplets.tail: Good optical quality but no myopia control effect

triplets.head: DOT Lenses (SightGlass)
triplets.tail: CYPRESS trial, n=256, North American, diverse

triplets.head: LARI Lenses
triplets.tail: Both +3.00 D and −3.00 D versions effective; no significant difference between them

triplets.head: Progressive Addition Lenses (PALs)
triplets.tail: Excluded from current myopia control protocols

triplets.head: Undercorrection of Myopia
triplets.tail: Does NOT slow and may accelerate progression; contraindicated

triplets.head: Atropine (general)
triplets.tail: Acts on retinal/scleral muscarinic receptors, dopamine modulation, NO signaling, scleral ECM remodeling inhibition; NOT primarily cycloplegia

triplets.head: Atropine (general)
triplets.tail: 1 drop/eye at bedtime, continued 2–3 years, gradual tapering

triplets.head: Atropine (general)
triplets.tail: No FDA-approved formulation as of 2025; available via compounding pharmacies only

triplets.head: Topical Caffeine 2%
triplets.tail: Did NOT slow progression as monotherapy

triplets.head: Lutein
triplets.tail: Improved macular pigment density in high myopes but no visual acuity improvement

triplets.head: Outdoor Time ≥2 hrs/day
triplets.tail: Strong for onset prevention; weaker for slowing progression in existing myopes

triplets.head: Red Light Therapy (RLRL)
triplets.tail: Photobiomodulation via cytochrome c oxidase → ATP, choroidal blood flow, dopamine/NO

triplets.head: Red Light Therapy (RLRL)
triplets.tail: Observed (0.42 mm vs 0.28 mm in 2-yr follow-up)

triplets.head: Blue Light Therapy (470 nm)
triplets.tail: One ongoing trial; very limited evidence

triplets.head: LASIK
triplets.tail: Flap-related complications, dry eye, ectasia risk

triplets.head: PRK
triplets.tail: More pain, slower recovery (1–3 weeks), haze risk (mitigated by mitomycin-C)

triplets.head: SMILE
triplets.tail: −0.5 to −10.0 D sphere, up to −3.0 D cylinder

triplets.head: ICL (Visian Phakic IOL)
triplets.tail: IOP elevation, cataract, endothelial cell loss

triplets.head: Refractive Surgery (general)
triplets.tail: Does NOT reduce lifetime risks of retinal detachment, maculopathy, or glaucoma

triplets.head: DIMS + 0.025% Atropine

PRK (Photorefractive Keratectomy)
triplets.tail: Mechanical debridement, brush, or dilute alcohol; epithelium discarded; regenerates under bandage contact lens

triplets.head: PRK (Photorefractive Keratectomy)
triplets.tail: Most discomfort of surface ablation types (3–5 days); slowest recovery (1–3 weeks functional)

triplets.head: LASEK
triplets.tail: Dilute alcohol (18–20%) applied 20–40 sec to loosen epithelium; peeled aside as thin flap; repositioned after ablation

triplets.head: LASEK
triplets.tail: Modestly less early discomfort; no significant final outcome difference by 6–12 months

triplets.head: LASEK
triplets.tail: Alcohol may cause transient limbal stem cell toxicity

triplets.head: LASEK
triplets.tail: Excimer laser (any platform) + alcohol solution + trephine/ring

triplets.head: Epi-LASIK
triplets.tail: Mechanical epithelial separator (epi-keratome) creates epithelial flap WITHOUT alcohol

triplets.head: Epi-LASIK
triplets.tail: Preserves more viable epithelial cells; avoids alcohol toxicity

triplets.head: TransPRK / SmartSurfACE
triplets.tail: No-touch, all-laser — excimer laser itself removes epithelium then continues to stromal ablation in a single step

triplets.head: TransPRK / SmartSurfACE
triplets.tail: Equivalent efficacy/safety; slightly better accuracy; faster healing; less pain; higher satisfaction

triplets.head: TransPRK / SmartSurfACE
triplets.tail: Specific excimer laser with integrated TransPRK software (SCHWIND AMARIS, Alcon EX500 StreamLight, or iVis iRES only)

triplets.head: A-1: Surface Ablation (all types)
triplets.tail: No significant differences in effectiveness, predictability, or safety among PRK, LASEK, Epi-LASIK by 6 months

triplets.head: A-1: Surface Ablation (all types)
triplets.tail: Less long-term dry eye; preferred for thin corneas, contact sports, anterior pathology

triplets.head: Conventional LASIK
triplets.tail: Standard Munnerlyn profile; sphere+cylinder only; changes cornea prolate→oblate; induces HOAs

triplets.head: Wavefront-Optimized (WFO) LASIK
triplets.tail: Extra peripheral pulses maintain prolate shape; prevents NEW HOAs but doesn't treat pre-existing ones; suitable for HOAs <0.4 μm; most widely used

triplets.head: Wavefront-Guided (WFG) LASIK
triplets.tail: Treats total ocular wavefront aberrations (measured by aberrometer); for HOAs >0.4 μm, glare/halos; requires repeatable aberrometry; superior contrast sensitivity

triplets.head: Topography-Guided (TG) LASIK
triplets.tail: Treats corneal surface irregularities (topographer data); FDA-approved for regular cornea + astigmatism; off-label for post-LASIK ectasia, decentered ablations

triplets.head: Femtosecond LASIK
triplets.tail: Excimer laser + femtosecond laser for flap creation

triplets.head: TG LASIK (Contoura)
triplets.tail: High-resolution corneal topographer (e.g., WaveLight Topolyzer VARIO)

triplets.head: LASIK (general)
triplets.tail: Flap issues (incomplete, buttonhole, striae, epithelial ingrowth, displacement), suction loss, OBL, dry eye, DLK, ectasia, glare/halos, regression

triplets.head: Class B: KLEx (general)
triplets.tail: Femtosecond laser creates intrastromal refractive lenticule; extracted through 2–5 mm incision; no excimer, no flap

triplets.head: Class B: KLEx (general)
triplets.tail: Preserves greater corneal biomechanics; less nerve damage/dry eye

triplets.head: CLEAR
triplets.tail: Intraoperative OCT; low pulse energy (<50 nJ)

triplets.head: KLEx (all platforms)
triplets.tail: Suction loss, difficult lenticule extraction, cap/side-cut tears, black spots, OBL, dry eye (less than LASIK), over/undercorrection, regression, vertical coma induction

triplets.head: KLEx (all platforms)
triplets.tail: No clinically significant differences between platforms in final outcomes despite parameter variations

triplets.head: WaveLight EX500
triplets.tail: WFO, WFG, TG (Contoura); StreamLight TransPRK mode

triplets.tail: STAR S4 IR excimer laser (WFG LASIK & PRK)
